title: Geometry - Lesson 4 Practice: Rectangle, Square, and Rhombus Problems
description: Practice comparing special parallelogram properties and solving basic side, angle, and diagonal problems.

questions.question: Which property always holds for every rectangle?
questions.explanation: A rectangle is defined as a parallelogram with four right angles.

questions.question: Which property always holds for every rhombus?
options: Only one pair of opposite sides is parallel.
questions.explanation: A rhombus is a parallelogram with four congruent sides.

questions.question: Every square is both a rectangle and a rhombus.
questions.explanation: A square has four right angles and four congruent sides, so it satisfies both definitions.

questions.question: In a rectangle, the diagonals are ______ in length.
questions.explanation: Rectangle diagonals are congruent, meaning they have equal length.

questions.question: A rhombus has diagonals that intersect at point E. If AE = 9 cm on diagonal AC, what is EC?
options: Cannot be determined because rhombus diagonals never bisect each other
questions.explanation: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so its diagonals bisect each other. Therefore AE = EC = 9 cm.

questions.question: A rhombus diagonal bisects an angle into two angles of 32 degrees each. The whole angle measures ______ degrees.
questions.explanation: The diagonal splits the angle into two equal parts, so 32 + 32 = 64 degrees.

questions.question: A student says, "This shape is a square because it looks like a square." Write a better way to justify that a parallelogram is a square.
questions.correctAnswer: Show that the parallelogram has both four right angles and four congruent sides, or show enough rectangle and rhombus properties to prove both conditions.
questions.explanation: Geometry classification should use definitions and measured or proven properties, not appearance.

questions.question: Compare the diagonals of a rectangle and a rhombus in one or two sentences.
questions.correctAnswer: Rectangle diagonals are congruent and bisect each other. Rhombus diagonals are perpendicular, bisect each other, and bisect opposite angles, but they are not always congruent.
questions.explanation: The shared property is diagonal bisection; the distinguishing properties are congruent diagonals for rectangles and perpendicular angle-bisecting diagonals for rhombuses.
